```markdown
# SEC filing-index ingestion — Roadmap

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`); uv workspace of four packages, with ingestion code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest` (spec §4.9); Azure platform per the ADR, still Proposed (spec §3 R4).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes over a chosen range, downloaded once with original bytes kept | §2.1, §3 R1, §4.2 | A | 1 | About 135 quarters from 1993 to the present. That is a few hundred SEC requests, minutes at 3 req/s. Bytes per quarter are measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily filing indexes picked up on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | §3 R2, §4.2 | A | 2 | About 250 daily files a year plus listings, negligible at 3 req/s |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet, parsed and validated from the ingested indexes, with provenance | §3 R3, §4.4–§4.6 | A | 3 | Rows and memory per quarter measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The whole system running on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor) | §3 R4, §4.1, §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend unknown until deployment, measured by Stage 7 |
| O5 | Backfill, daily and reconciliation runs using one downloader, parser and publisher, differing only in which sources they select | §3 R5, §4.1–§4.2 | A | 5 | Engineering time only |
| O6 | Any stored index re-parsed after a parser change, with no new SEC download | §3 R6, §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage grows by one raw copy per snapshot. Size measured by Stage 1 |
| O7 | Later changes to quarterly indexes reconciled into the catalog, with source history kept | §3 R7, §4.2, §4.4 | A | 7 | One weekly re-read of all supported quarters, the same request count as O1 |
| O8 | All SEC traffic through one downloader and one request budget, however many workers run | §3 R8, §4.3 | A | 8 | Engineering time only |
| O9 | Readers get each quarter's current dataset through one versioned manifest and active pointer | §3 R9, §4.5–§4.6 | A | 9 | Engineering time only |
| O10 | Records leave the catalog only after explicit, hash-bound approval of a closed-quarter replacement | §3 R10, §4.4 | A | 10 | Operator time per gated candidate |
| O11 | Schedules, retry limits and rate target as validated, reviewable configuration | §3 R11, §4.8, §5 | A | 11 | Engineering time only |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: One real quarter, end to end, locally
      Objective: Download one real archived quarterly master index and turn it into canonical Parquet on local disk.
      Outcomes: O1 (one quarter), O3
      Consumes: nothing (generated package scaffolds only)
      Produces: the downloader with SEC identity and a 3 req/s limit; raw bytes kept with SHA-256; the parser and the sec-index-v1 row contract (§4.5) as a local Parquet writer; specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: one real archived quarter is fetched with an identifying User-Agent at no more than 3 req/s, and its raw bytes are kept under their SHA-256. O3: that quarter yields sec-index-v1 Parquet, and malformed rows are refused, not dropped. The findings file records the byte count, row count, elapsed time, peak memory and request count of the real run.
      Leaves out: source manifest and replay (Stage 2); shared lease, retry policy and config validation (Stage 3); daily indexes, backfill range and historical-format fixtures (Stage 4); generations, manifests and pointer (Stage 5); reconciliation and withdrawals (Stage 6); Azure, scheduling and deployment (Stages 7–8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 2: Source manifest and replay
      Objective: Keep durable source, snapshot, processing and attempt state, and re-parse stored inputs without the SEC.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader, raw store and parser
      Produces: source manifest records and the downloaded → transformed → published states (§4.5); per-source checkpoints and worksets (§4.1–§4.2); observation output keyed by snapshot, parser and schema; replay from raw storage
      Exit: O6: after a parser-version change, re-processing a stored snapshot makes zero SEC requests and yields a new processing identity; unchanged hash and versions are a no-op; a partial run resumes without redoing completed members.
      Leaves out: Table Storage and ADLS bindings (Stage 7); publication manifest (Stage 5)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Shared SEC access and configuration
      Objective: Put every SEC request behind one lease-held request budget, with the stated retry policy and validated configuration.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: Stage 1's downloader; Stage 2's attempt records
      Produces: coordination behind an interface, with a local implementation; bounded retries, Retry-After handling and a halt on access denial (§5); typed config (`conf/sec-edgar-ingest.yaml`) refused before any I/O when invalid
      Exit: O8: concurrent collectors in CI never overlap as request issuers, retries count toward the budget, and lease loss stops new requests. O11: every §4.8 key validates, and each §5 configuration error is refused before any network request.
      Leaves out: the Storage-backed lease and ADF schedules (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Backfill range and daily ingestion
      Objective: Run backfill over a configured range and daily ingestion with catch-up, as source selections over the shared pipeline.
      Outcomes: O1 (configured range), O2, O5
      Consumes: Stages 1–3
      Produces: the `discover` and `collect` commands for backfill and daily runs; `index.json` discovery; golden fixtures for the historical formats in the chosen range; run reports with gaps and `no_new_sources`
      Exit: O1: backfill over a fixture range reports complete, pending and failed units separately. O2: CI covers quarter boundaries, a missed run and a multi-quarter outage, and a failed listing does not advance the checkpoint. O5: backfill and daily runs share the same downloader, parser and transform code.
      Leaves out: publication (Stage 5); reconciliation (Stage 6); scheduling (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned quarter publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation behind a conditionally updated active pointer.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 2's processing states; Stage 4's observations
      Produces: the `publish` command; generation layout, manifest.json and changes.parquet (§4.5); a pointer store interface with conditional writes and a local implementation; precedence and dedup for additions and updates (§4.4)
      Exit: O9: in CI, with crashes injected before files finish, before the pointer update and just after it, readers see only complete generations; competing publishers lose no update; repeated inputs produce no duplicate logical records.
      Leaves out: the withdrawal gate (Stage 6); Table Storage binding (Stage 7)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly sources, apply safe changes, and gate withdrawals behind hash-bound approval.
      Outcomes: O7, O10
      Consumes: Stages 4–5
      Produces: the reconciliation source selection; approval records; `awaiting_approval` candidates
      Exit: O7: additions and field updates publish with recorded changes, and open-quarter absence withdraws nothing. O10: a closed-quarter removal stays gated until approval names its exact source hash and candidate; a stale daily replay cannot resurrect a withdrawn key; a later quarterly reintroduction is recorded.
      Leaves out: operator approval runbook (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure platform in an isolated environment
      Objective: Run the shared worker on Azure under ADF, with managed identities, under version-controlled infrastructure and with triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6
      Produces: container image and pinned digest; ADLS, Table Storage and lease bindings; ADF pipelines with job start and poll; structured logs and alerts (§4.7); `infra/azure/sec-edgar-ingest/`
      Exit: O4: the integration tests in §6 pass in an isolated environment. The live smoke test and raw-storage replay (§7 steps 3–5) are recorded with byte counts, row counts, elapsed time, peak memory, request rate, image digest and Azure cost.
      Leaves out: production triggers and baseline campaign (Stage 8)
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Production baseline and scheduled operation
      Objective: Run the baseline and catch-up in production, enable the daily and reconciliation triggers, and exercise the runbooks.
      Outcomes: O1, O2, O7 at production standard
      Consumes: Stage 7's deployed platform; owner-approved range, handoff date and SEC identity (§7 step 1)
      Produces: active quarter generations; release record; `docs/runbooks/`
      Exit: O1: every requested baseline unit is published, or the approved incomplete range is recorded. O2: the daily trigger is enabled after an accepted catch-up, and observed scheduled runs match their reports. O7: one manual reconciliation is run, its gates are resolved, and the weekly trigger is enabled.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: writing-plans

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11, with evidence for each verdict (implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Also list as unmet any of R1–R11 that no outcome's Spec cell cites. Each unmet item exits as a new stage or as a recorded deferral with a written reason. Then retire the roadmap, the spec and the ADR to `specs/completed/`.
```
